Boundary redesign research at package checkpoint30e211dae891cfdca3f6322ce45c46c426138830, October6 2026. User asks whether larger coherent Rust ports and adjacent package code can remove the issues rather than mechanically preserve earlier helper boundaries. Scope remains existing packages/ features, no compiler modifications, language-named folders forbidden. We may propose new private input contracts while keeping existing public APIs; do not silently restrict legacy inputs. No Rust prototype or new benchmarks/tests exist. Earlier ratings7 arithmetic/5 complete unknown validation/7 work decisions/7 artifact helpers describe different, smaller scopes and are not evidence of a redesigned path's feasibility.
Values: combine exact arithmetic/carriers, runtime type AST/prepared ordered plans, wire decode/validation/normalization/encode. Normalized field ASTs exist but leaves and union arms reparse. HTTP operations creates fresh JSON/form data before framing/bound checks; interfaces/mcp bound checker is a real whole-input consumer and now delegates datetime to values. Generic public unknown/in-process/MCP calls are not thereby inert. Parser-owned snapshots can exclude getters/proxies/holes/functions/cycles at a new proven internal boundary, with legacy unknown APIs retaining TS observable reads. JSON still permits escaped lone UTF16 surrogates, numeric values, own proto keys and JS ordering; preserve text, presence and exact number/error policies. Can opaque json rejects all numbers, so it is not a generic transport DTO. Combine decode/check/encode or aggregates in one call; Rust handles only help while actual consumers keep work in Rust, current generated JS needs BigInts/structural fields so no free scalar-chain benefit. Preserving every old export leaves getter/identity costs. State admission reads revision/raw canonical hash and receipt replay before age/auth/input validation; never normalize/hash decoded defaults earlier. Interfaces framing first-error/own-presence differs from values collected violations and state positive15digit version convention. Legacy stableStringify supports toJSON/getters, JS numeric rendering/UTF16 key sorting; a new parsed-data codec can narrow its domain, old behavior must remain.
Work: kernel row codecs and state fanout tables restate shapes; state outcome/checkpoint staging mirrors work lifecycle behavior; Cloudflare durable claim/record adapters implement production sequencing while work memory store is test-only. A shared Rust core can own ordered row codecs, transitions, receipt projections, recovery and commit-batch linkage assertions; retain package owners and public error profiles. TS host obtains DB rows/membership/provider/guards and performs fenced commit. First consolidate matching rules/contract facts rather than treat different outer orders as equal. Next a request/resume Rust session can request load/query/checkpoint/snapshot/guard/authority/invoke and return expected-version/revision batch, retaining state between requests. It must preserve callback demand/order, exceptions, single-shot commit, race rereads and caller-controlled retries. Moving complete DB/auth/providers adds scope rather than removing these constraints. State query uses declarative predicates but viewer projection precedes user where, sorting includes JS/f64 behavior and limit overflow errors; migration invariants execute JS callbacks. These adjacent row folds are later candidates with safeguards, not automatically exact-values algorithms.
Artifacts: current local helpers run in one JS process already. A Rust helper-by-helper port would introduce crossings; a native prepare operation can own artifact/release tree+module graph+compatibility+plans/diffs/JSON/TOML review and byte-safe staged output. Preserve additive artifact metadata, first errors, JSON text/surrogates, plan/reason/resource order, JS escaping, current hash formats and unmapped schedules. Existing manifest already hashes arbitrary dist bytes. Current bundle invokes Bun for actual MCP JS and calls owner interfaces catalog derivation to bake derived-inputs.js; replacing JS parser/bundler or duplicating owner rules is not needed. Consume prebuilt outputs or one coarse JS build adapter, retaining native graph/buffers and returning review metadata/bytes. One extra parse in build adapter may remain. Keep activation producer gates and Wrangler apply outside the native prepare tranche. Preview currently writes no deployment files; preserve prepare/review/write/apply ordering and exact content identity. Native distribution is additional work and small helpers alone have little proven benefit. Typed text/Wasm asset plumbing plus module-scope initialization and real workerd test improves values/work even if preparation remains TS. Existing JS-only binary loader limitations are bounded but unproved. Native tools and Worker runtime need different host adapters. Node hashing is already native; no performance superiority is demonstrated.

values_boundary.instructions: Which next migration boundary for values arithmetic and validation best reduces interop and duplicate semantic ownership while preserving complete workflows and legacy behavior, with manageable adoption/maintenance? Compare options fairly; expected speed is unproven. Assess boundary strategy, not a mandate to port.

criteria.owned_pipeline: Combine exact types/math/ordered prepared plans and whole checks/encoding for a new parser-owned inert input path; retain legacy unknown JS adapters. Real HTTP/interfaces consumers and fewer internal conversions, but two input profiles, lossless-text/binary work and TS comparator remain.
criteria.legacy_full_port: Combine the same core but port every existing export/input unchanged, including observable reads, output identity and synchronous wrappers. Complete semantic replacement and native reuse, but host evaluation protocol remains and widening does not remove it.
criteria.ts_preparation: Keep values TS, prepare AST/leaf/union plans and use whole-input existing callers; establish workload evidence first. Lowest build/boundary cost and preserves legacy semantics, but no native reuse or Rust data ownership.

work_boundary.instructions: Which next migration boundary for work/state lifecycle and recovery best reduces interop and duplicate semantic ownership while preserving complete workflows and legacy behavior, with manageable adoption/maintenance? Compare options fairly; expected speed is unproven. Assess boundary strategy, not a mandate to port.

criteria.transition_core: Share work/state row codecs, lifecycle/outcome/checkpoint/receipt/recovery policy and conditional batch linkage; preserve host orchestration, error profiles and fences. Removes real mirrors with contained migration, but callbacks and boundary snapshots remain.
criteria.resumable_commands: Also move command/scheduler control into retained Rust request/resume sessions with TS host I/O. More state ownership and fewer orchestration mirrors; larger protocol, exception/retry/sequence verification cost.
criteria.whole_runtime: Move work engine plus DB/membership/auth/invocation/provider integration broadly into Rust. Fewer inter-language seams and more native authority, but broad platform/security/transaction scope and excluded generated handlers constrain it.
criteria.ts_consolidation: Consolidate row/policy duplicates in TS and keep host execution. Minimal distribution cost and useful consistency; postpones shared native policy and does not evaluate Rust economics.

artifact_boundary.instructions: Which next migration boundary for local artifact and deployment preparation best reduces interop and duplicate semantic ownership while preserving complete workflows and legacy behavior, with manageable adoption/maintenance? Compare options fairly; expected speed is unproven. Assess boundary strategy, not a mandate to port.

criteria.owned_preparation: One native local prepare operation owning artifact/release/graph/check/plan/review/staging, consuming prebuilt JS or one coarse owner build adapter; retain activation/Wrangler. Coherent ownership and binary reuse, with native release/byte/diagnostic parity work.
criteria.helper_exports: Rust ports of current parsed-artifact/compatibility/plan helpers through TS wrappers. Smaller steps and easy rollout, but introduces crossings/materialization while TS still owns the workflow.
criteria.full_platform: Replace platform CLI, JS build tooling and Worker/deployment integrations in Rust. Broad native ownership, high scope and package/callback/host complexity without demonstrated necessity.
criteria.ts_asset_upgrade: Keep local preparation TS and add typed binary asset/loading/manifests for runtime cores. Lowest local port cost and enables Wasm; no native preparation reuse.
